# Requirements Quality Checklist: Raise to Power Operation

**Purpose**: Validate completeness, clarity and consistency of the error-handling and backend-parity requirements
**Created**: 2026-11-19
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are input requirements defined for how base and exponent are entered (number format, empty or non-numeric input)? [Gap, Spec §FR-001] <!-- Assumptions: input follows existing operations -->
- [x] CHK002 Are the allowed ranges of base and exponent specified, or is it stated that they follow existing operand limits? [Gap, Spec §Assumptions] <!-- Assumptions: existing operand limits -->
- [x] CHK003 Is the UI exposure of the operation (label, position, tooltip) specified beyond "consistently"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006] <!-- FR-006 now specifies button, label, tooltip -->
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements defined for error state recovery (e.g. what the result display shows after an error and the next calculation)? [Gap, Spec §US2] <!-- Assumptions: same as existing operations -->
- [x] CHK005 Are keyboard and accessibility requirements for the new operation control stated or explicitly excluded? [Gap, Spec §FR-006] <!-- FR-006: same as other buttons -->

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is "clear error" fully defined by the exact messages for every failure class? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005] <!-- FR-005 exact messages -->
- [ ] CHK007 Is "exact where representable" defined, including what representable means for the decimal result type? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-002] <!-- Open: "exactly representable" is not defined; decide if integer results are exact only within decimal range -->
- [ ] CHK008 Is "too large" defined with a measurable threshold, given the backends have different limits? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-005] <!-- Open: no numeric threshold for "too large"; give per-backend limits (about 7.9e28 in-process, below 1e20 database) in the spec or README -->
- [ ] CHK009 Is it clear how "12 significant digits" applies to results near zero or to very large values? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004] <!-- Open: 12-digit rule near zero/very large not defined; consider relative error -->
- [x] CHK010 Is "same number of steps" in SC-001 defined with a concrete count or flow? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001] <!-- SC-001 now concrete -->

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK011 Are the edge-case statement "division by zero" and the message "Cannot raise zero to a negative power" consistent? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-005] <!-- Edge case wording kept; message defined in FR-005 -->
- [x] CHK012 Does the "same results on both backends" requirement stay consistent with any documented range limits of the database backend? [Conflict, Spec §FR-004] <!-- FR-004 now requires documenting range differences -->
- [x] CHK013 Is the precedence between error classes defined when an input matches more than one (e.g. zero base, negative fractional exponent)? [Gap, Spec §FR-005] <!-- Edge Cases: precedence added -->
- [x] CHK014 Is the existing overflow message reconciled with the new "Result is too large" wording? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005] <!-- FR-005: replaces overflow wording for power only -->

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK015 Are the "defined valid test cases" and "defined invalid cases" enumerated so SC-002 and SC-003 can be measured? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, §SC-003] <!-- Open: test case list lives in contract/quickstart, not referenced from the spec -->
- [x] CHK016 Does each user story acceptance scenario map to a stated requirement ID? [Traceability, Spec §US1-US3] <!-- each scenario maps to FR-001..FR-005; accepted -->
- [x] CHK017 Does US3 scenario 2 specify that messages, not only error occurrence, match across backends? [Consistency, Spec §US3, §FR-005] <!-- US3 scenario 2 now requires same message -->

## Edge Case & Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK018 Are edge cases addressed for zero and negative-zero exponents, base 1, base -1, and very small fractional results? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases] <!-- Edge Cases: base 1, -1 added -->
- [x] CHK019 Are requirements defined for results that round to zero (underflow)? [Gap, Spec §FR-002] <!-- Edge Cases: underflow rounds to 0 -->
- [x] CHK020 Are requirements defined for the database backend being unavailable during a power calculation? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Gap] <!-- Assumptions: existing unavailable error -->

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK021 Is the assumption that precision and formatting follow existing operations validated against fractional results with many digits? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions] <!-- Open: only validated by tests, not by a spec statement -->
- [x] CHK022 Is the documentation requirement scoped to specific files beyond "wherever operations are listed"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, §SC-004] <!-- accepted; README is the only doc listing operations -->

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
